subject: history
title: Great Terror and the Great Patriotic War
welcome_lead: From the show trials of 1936 to victory in 1945, study the years that defined Stalinism and the Soviet experience of WWII.
meta_desc: History Soviet Union Adventure 3: Great Terror 1936-38 and the Great Patriotic War 1941-45.
final_note: You have walked through fear and sacrifice. Stalin's death in March 1953 closed the era but his legacy remained contested.

walkthroughs.body_html: The murder of Kirov in 1934 served as pretext for escalating repression. The trials of Zinoviev and Kamenev (1936), Pyatakov (1937) and Bukharin (1938) liquidated Old Bolsheviks. The Yezhovshchina under NKVD chief Nikolai Yezhov (1936-38) extended quotas of arrests and executions throughout Soviet society, including the army and ethnic groups.

Operation Barbarossa on 22 June 1941 caught Stalin by surprise. Despite catastrophic initial losses, the USSR rallied: the defence of Moscow (1941), the encirclement at Stalingrad (winter 1942-43), the tank battle at Kursk (1943) and the relief of Leningrad (January 1944) turned the tide. The Red Army reached Berlin in April-May 1945.

Soviet losses reached an estimated 27 million dead. Post-war Stalin reasserted ideological orthodoxy, deported nationalities, launched the Zhdanovshchina against intellectuals and pursued antisemitic campaigns including the Doctors' Plot of 1953. He died on 5 March 1953, opening the way for the Khrushchev era and partial de-Stalinisation.

mcqs.q: What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.

mcqs.q: Why did Henry II clash with Thomas Becket?
options: The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
They quarrelled because Becket wanted to be Pope.
Becket resisted Henry's attempt to bring 'criminous clerks' under royal courts via the Constitutions of Clarendon, defending Church independence from royal jurisdiction.
Henry II ordered Becket's assassination personally.

mcqs.q: What was the theory of the four humours?
options: They quarrelled because Becket wanted to be Pope.
Disease was caused by imbalance of blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile; treatment aimed to rebalance them via bloodletting, purging or diet. It dominated for nearly 2,000 years.
Medieval doctors knew about germs but used humours because they had no medicine.
The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
